concerns.text: The plan relies on a 'Verified Datasets' block citing 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/latentskill/weights' as a 'Hypothetical Verified Source'. The LatentSkill paper (arXiv:2606.06087) does not provide a public, programmatic dataset of pre-trained LoRA A/B matrices for ALFWorld/Search-QA. Without access to the ground-truth weight vectors for the 'known composite tasks' required to calculate reconstruction error (SC-005) and validate text-weight alignment (FR-007), the core hypothesis (linearity of latent space) cannot be empirically tested. The research question is unanswerable with the proposed data source.

Phase 2 proposes running 'N=10 independent simulations' on a 2-core CPU runner with 7GB RAM for Llama-3-8B (4-bit) + ALFWorld environment. This is computationally infeasible. Loading a 4-bit 8B model (~5-6GB) leaves <1GB for the environment logic, sentence-transformers, and Python overhead, guaranteeing OOM. Furthermore, running 10 full inference passes per task for 20 tasks (200+ runs) on a 2-core CPU will exceed the 6-hour performance goal and likely the runner's execution timeout, making the statistical power (FR-008) unachievable as planned.

The plan assumes 'text-weight alignment' (FR-007) can be validated by correlating text embeddings with weight vectors. However, without the ground-truth weights for the *composite* tasks (which are synthesized in the plan), the 'reconstruction error' (SC-005) cannot be calculated. The plan conflates 'synthesizing' a weight vector via interpolation with 'validating' it against a ground truth. If the ground truth weights for the composite tasks do not exist (as implied by the lack of a public dataset), the linearity assumption cannot be validated, only the *performance* of the synthesized weights can be measured, which is a different claim.
